summary: Clear, useful support email. Optional low-priority improvement: group the refund scope with its pending status, then end with the promised update and fallback. Conventional courtesy is not itself a defect. Supplied origin: AI-authored synthetic fixture. Existing native scores are uncalibrated experimental model outputs, not verified authorship.

document_analysis.structure: P1/P5 frame the email. P2 gives request status and empathy, P3 conditions and customer action, P4 follow-up followed by payment-scope limits. Returning to payment scope after the follow-up is a small organization opportunity.
document_analysis.reasoning_specificity: P2-P4 distinguish confirmed payment, submitted request, pending approval, estimated arrival, and a firm update deadline. These are different facts and commitments, not repetitive hedging.
document_analysis.voice_consistency: Alex consistently uses first person for actions within Alex's control and the payment team for approval. Formal warmth fits support correspondence.
document_analysis.rhythm_repetition: P2 opens with thanks and closes with empathy/apology. This familiar service pattern may feel templated but performs a legitimate interpersonal function. P3's two conditional/timing sentences distinguish conditions; no excessive repetition is established.
document_analysis.language_features: Plain professional English, conventional greeting/signoff and explicit conditions. No grammar, idiom, or unusual register problem is evident.
document_analysis.citations_provenance: No citations are requested or needed. sources.json labels the email an AI-authored synthetic fixture, not actual payment/customer history. Hash binding identifies the supplied text, not a real transaction.

spans.quote: Thank you for your patience while I reviewed the duplicate charge on order R-214. I confirmed that the second payment was taken on 18 September. I submitted a refund request for £36 this morning, but the payment team has not approved it yet. I understand why seeing two charges would be frustrating, and I am sorry for the extra work this has caused you.
